rooms.name: Luna River Crossroads
rooms.desc: Four roads meet at an X on a low wooded shoulder. The gravel of the Old Svalich Road crunches underfoot; the track to the north-west and the trail to the south-east are turf and dirt. In the eastern elbow the stump of a snapped signpost leans out of its stones; its top lies in the weeds a few paces off.
rooms.dm: Always roll a random encounter on arriving here, day or night (tables p.29); stage it with the placements on this map. The signpost is a free clue: rejoined, its arms give Krezk and Tsolenka Pass SW, Lake Baratok NW, Vallaki and Ravenloft NE, Berez SE; this is one of the signs Urwin Martikov tells wine-fetchers to follow (p.98). Travel at 3 mph: Vallaki's Sunset Gate about a mile NE over the bridge (20 min); Krezk about 5 miles SW (under 2 hr); the NW branch is a dirt trail within half a mile, throws off the path to Van Richten's Tower and rejoins the Old Svalich Road after a couple of miles; Berez about 4 miles down the SE trail (2 hr), which ends in marsh. The Argynvostholt branch leaves the road a mile or so SW.

rooms.name: The weeds and the drag furrow
rooms.desc: Nettle, dock and dead thistle crowd the wedge between the two eastern roads where the post once stood clear. A furrow of flattened stems runs from the stump to the Berez trail.
rooms.dm: Survival DC 12 reads the story: oversized wolf prints round the stump and along the furrow, a wheel gouge and a hoop scrape. A dire wolf pack ran a wine cart off the road; the post went with it. The cask lies in the ditch west of the X.

rooms.name: The wolf-skull pine
rooms.desc: An old pine in the north elbow wears a column of wolf skulls nailed up its trunk, the topmost still in its hide. The skulls click together when the wind gets under them.
rooms.dm: A trappers' tally, like the wolf heads on pikes outside Vallaki's gates (p.95). Werewolves in human form posing as trappers (p.33) fit here: one stands under the tree and hails the party, the others within whistling distance up the track; they want to know who carries silver.

rooms.name: The cask in the ditch
rooms.desc: A smashed wine cask and a cart's tailboard lie in the north ditch of the road, staves and a hoop strewn up the bank, a wheel gouge torn in the verge. The cart is gone; the mess is not.
rooms.dm: The Wizard of Wines' overdue delivery for the Blue Water Inn (p.98): the staves carry the winery's burned mark (Investigation DC 10 also finds 7 cp in a pouch under the tailboard). A party sent for the shipment learns it was lost on this road; that can lead on to the winery. Needle blights lurch out of the pines south of the road here.

rooms.name: The Baratok cart-track
rooms.desc: A grassed cart-track climbs north-west in a sunken lane between root-bound banks, turf between its ruts and needles in them. A hundred feet on, the gravel is gone and the trees close in as it bends west.
rooms.dm: To Lake Baratok and Van Richten's Tower (V). The druid with twig blights comes down this track on all fours; the blights swarm the banks (half cover on the bank tops, which are 3-4 ft high).

rooms.name: The Berez trail and the corduroy
rooms.desc: The trail to Berez drops off the shoulder as a ribbon of dirt and crosses the boggy knoll foot on a causeway of half-sunk pine logs. Hoofprints only; boots drum hollow on the logs.
rooms.dm: The corduroy is difficult terrain (slick, uneven logs); off the logs the bog is knee-deep mud. Zombies coming up from Berez stumble here. The trail hugs the river south for about 4 miles before it turns to marsh.

rooms.name: The hay terrace
rooms.desc: A wet, open flood terrace between the forest and the river: tussock grass once cut for hay, reeds in the hollows, black water standing in old cart ruts, a few drowned alders. The only open sky for a mile.
rooms.dm: Wolves own this ground at night. Scarecrows up from Berez hunting ravens stand among the reeds between the rick and the carcass (passive Perception 11 sees one lurch; otherwise surprise). The rick is dry cover from rain and nothing else.

rooms.name: The west causeway
rooms.desc: The road climbs onto a raised gravel causeway across the wet terrace, black-water ditches either side, a weathered painted board leaning at its west end. Fog lies here at dawn.
rooms.dm: Vistani bandits lounge here by day (they offer to guide for 100 gp); dire wolves step out of the fog here by night. The board carries the burgomaster's festival slogan (p.98).

rooms.name: The Luna bridge
rooms.desc: A low arching bridge of mossy grey stone: a broad main arch over the river and a small flood arch over the dry gully beside it. Waist-high parapets, a deck fifteen feet wide, wheel grooves packed with mud. Ravens sit on the parapet.
rooms.dm: Sound and old. The flood arch is a dry crawl-through hide for anything Medium or smaller. Strahd zombies wait on the shoal under the main arch and climb the pier when someone steps onto the span. Bats boil out from under both arches at dusk. About 1,050 ft from the X; Vallaki's gate is about a mile on.

rooms.name: The east bank
rooms.desc: The far bank rises steeply out of the water into unbroken forest toward Vallaki.
rooms.dm: Strahd's wolves watch who crosses toward Vallaki: after dark, dire wolf eye-shine among these trees (passive Perception 14). Wolves call from here first at night; the answer comes from the south down the Berez trail.

objects.label: The Luna River
objects.desc: A dark, slow river forty feet wide, sliding south in a trench below sedge banks; no rapids, no sound but a low hush.

objects.label: Weeds in the eastern elbow
objects.desc: A ragged wedge of nettle, dock and dead thistle between the two eastern roads, a flattened furrow dragged through it toward the Berez trail.

objects.label: Snapped signpost
objects.desc: The lower half of a stout oak post, splintered off about four feet up and leaning out of its packing of field stones toward the river.

objects.label: The signpost's top half
objects.desc: The top of the signpost lies face-up in the weeds: a short shaft with four carved arms, their painted letters flaking white on grey. One arm is cracked and points at the sky.

objects.label: Oversized wolf prints in the furrow mud (Survival DC 12)
objects.playerLabel: Big paw prints in the mud
objects.dm: Dire wolf prints, a cart wheel's gouge and a cask-hoop scrape: a dire wolf pack ran a wine cart off the road at the X; the post went with it, and the cask ended in the ditch to the west.

objects.label: The wolf-skull pine
objects.desc: A big old pine with a column of wolf skulls nailed up its trunk, a dozen of them, the highest still wearing its hide. Rows of knife notches score the bark beside them.

objects.label: Fresh notches and a skull still wet (trappers within the week)
objects.playerLabel: A fresh skull on the pine
objects.dm: Barovian trappers thinning Strahd's wolves passed here within the week. The werewolves who pose as trappers (p.33) stand under exactly this tree. If the hunting-trap result is rolled, the trap lies under the needles where travellers cut the corner from the track (DC 15 Survival, front rank).

objects.label: Smashed cask in the ditch
objects.desc: A burst wine cask and a cart's tailboard lie in the ditch, hoop and staves strewn up the bank, and a raw gouge shows where a wheel went off the road.

objects.label: Branded staves; 7 cp in a pouch under the tailboard (Investigation DC 10)
objects.dm: The staves are burned with the Wizard of Wines' mark: this is the overdue delivery Urwin Martikov is waiting on at the Blue Water Inn (p.98). The carter's purse holds 7 cp.

objects.label: The knoll crown
objects.desc: A knob of lichen-blotched granite breaking through the needles, ringed by the oldest pines on the map. Its top is dry and flat, ankle-deep in old needles.

objects.label: Root-bound bank
objects.desc: The track runs sunken between earth banks shoulder-high to a dwarf, pine roots looping out of their faces.

objects.label: Corduroy logs
objects.desc: Eighty feet of pine logs laid side by side across a bog, half sunk and slick, mossy at their uphill ends; the mud sucks at the gaps between them.

objects.label: Collapsed hay rick
objects.desc: Last season's hay rick, grey and slumped, its thatch cap slid off into the grass and a pitchfork still stuck in its side.

objects.label: Skinned wolf
objects.desc: A grey wolf skinned for its pelt and left, two crossbow bolts still in its ribs, in a stain of trampled mud ringed with big paw prints. It reeks.

objects.label: Ravens
objects.desc: Ravens working at the carcass; they hop off a few yards when anyone comes near.

objects.label: Reed hollow
objects.desc: Reeds standing in a hollow of black water on the terrace.

objects.label: Painted board
objects.desc: A weathered board on a post at the end of the causeway, painted with Vallaki's festival slogan; half the letters have flaked away.

objects.label: The Luna bridge
objects.desc: A low stone bridge of mossy ashlar on two arches, a wide one over the river and a small one over the dry gully beside it; waist-high parapets, wheel grooves full of mud, a raised gravel causeway at either end.

objects.dm: Comes bounding down the cart-track on all fours, then stops on the crown to sniff and laugh. Flees toward Yester Hill when all its blights fall or at half hit points. (Staged on the crown level; move it there.)

objects.label: North-east over the bridge: Vallaki's Sunset Gate about a mile on (20 minutes), wolf heads on pikes outside it.
South-west: the Old Svalich Road to Krezk (S), about 5 miles, level; the Argynvostholt branch (Q) leaves it a mile or so on.
North-west: the cart-track toward Lake Baratok and Van Richten's Tower (V); a dirt trail within half a mile.
South-east: the trail to the ruins of Berez (U), about 4 miles along the river, ending in marsh.
North, up the river gap: the grey gleam of Lake Zarovich. The river is swimmable but cold and dark: Athletics DC 10, 6-10 ft deep, slow.

From the crown: the bridge, the river gap, a gleam of Lake Zarovich to the north, and Argynvostholt's spur SSW across the valley (its beacon shows from here once lit, p.130). The best camp: dry, high, a defensible rock.

rooms.name: The knoll crown
rooms.desc: A dry, still knob of granite above the trees' lower boughs, lichen crunching underfoot and old needles ankle-deep in its hollows. Over the canopy to the north-east the pale double arch of the bridge shows above the river gap.
rooms.dm: Lookout and the best camp on the map: half cover at its lip, and the ledges on its south-east face are the only easy way up (a scramble). The druid stops here to sniff and laugh. Wolves will not rush the rock; they wait.

rooms.name: The Luna River
rooms.desc: Cold, dark water forty feet wide sliding south out of the lake basin, slow and steady, six to ten feet deep in the middle. Sedge banks rise ten feet either side; at dawn the fog fills the trench.
rooms.dm: Swimming: Strength (Athletics) DC 10 and wet gear; never more than 10 ft deep, even at Berez (p.161). The banks are a scramble (DC 10 Athletics, or use the bridge). Downstream it reaches Berez in about 4 miles.

rooms.name: The shoal under the arch
rooms.desc: A bar of gravel under the main arch's west footing, knee-deep water round it, a drowned alder snag caught on its upstream end with a drift of dead leaves behind it. The arch's underside is close overhead.
rooms.dm: A dry place to stand under the bridge. Strahd zombies wait here at night and climb the pier when someone steps onto the span. Bats roost in the arch. The flood mark on the pier's upstream face and a fisherman's abandoned trap are found from here.

objects.label: Gravel shoal and snag
objects.desc: A gravel bar under the arch with a drowned alder caught on it and a drift of leaves on its upstream side.

objects.label: Flood mark on the pier (6 ft above the water)
objects.playerLabel: A line scored on the pier
objects.dm: A scored line and a chiselled notch on the upstream cutwater, six feet above today's water, dead reed jammed in the joints at that height: the river ran that high the night Strahd swelled it to drown Berez (p.161).

objects.label: Rotted fish trap at the pier footing: line and an iron hook
objects.dm: A Vallaki fisherman's abandoned set: a willow trap, a coil of sound line and an iron hook. Only seen from the shoal or the water.

objects.label: Strahd zombie (on the shoal; 1d8 in all)
objects.playerLabel: A sutured corpse under the bridge
objects.dm: Strahd zombies (1d8, night): waiting on the gravel shoal under the main arch, they climb the pier footing when the party steps onto the span. A quiet party without lights can try to hide.
